summary: Built both milestones. M1: the flood live loop (floods/live.py) runs as a second asyncio task in the API lifespan (off with FIRE3D_FLOODS=0; a flood failure never reaches the fire loop), rebuilds the flood list every 15 min, spends at most 20 upstream requests a cycle on a background prefetch (product-text H-VTEC, zone outlines, member gauge series; NWS calls on NWS_LIMITER), appends new NWS product versions and gauge readings to ready bundles (every version kept, manifest.refreshed_ms), queues refresh jobs when NASA has a newer satellite pass or NWS a new forecast-map time, and auto-builds the 4 most severe floods once. /api/floods/status answers from the loop (counts null when the lists fail). CLI catalog --hazard flood and build-flood; check_bundle --hazard flood; SPEC 8.9. M2 (cut line, U1 (a)): past floods (floods/history.py). A bulk IEM route with H-VTEC severity, damage tags and emergencies exists (watchwarn.py CSV with follow-up statements + sbw_interval polygons), so the year lists follow PAST_RULE (moderate_or_worse), not the fallback; built once per year in the background (2025: 1,976 floods from 24 IEM + 5 map requests in 23 s; 2026: 2,108), cached for good for 2025, ids from the registry so live floods keep their ids; the detail chain's year step; archived NWS products and USGS readings with today's thresholds at past times. Gates green: backend 1383 passed, 0 skipped; web typecheck, lint 55 warnings (all src/scene), 1706 tests passed, build. REVIEW FIXES (BFL-R1..R10, all fixed; docs/redesign/reports/review5-backend-flood-live.json): one budget a cycle for the prefetch and the append step (NWS and NWPS together); due refreshes warmed at a pace that leaves NWPS room and run by the loop's own runner, never the job workers; a refresh never makes a bundle worse (members, NWPS detail, model series and ok layers kept when the rebuild cannot load them again, REFRESH_KEPT in the manifest); satellite pass keys tried kept on disk; product texts refused by Fire-3d's own limit asked again; year rows use each product's own time and the newest product's end, leave out floods still in effect, follow aliases and live VTEC keys, name the issuing office; a past flood answers 409 PAST_NO_BUNDLE to Prepare and never today's model output.

known_issues: Refresh jobs re-run the whole flood build (build.py is not this role's file); terrain comes from the HTTP cache, so a refresh takes 1-40 s, and built_ms changes (the web reloads the bundle). What a rebuild cannot load again is kept from the earlier build (review BFL-R1).

A past (year-list) flood is never prepared as a 3D bundle: POST build answers 409 PAST_NO_BUNDLE (an at_ms-aware build would need build.py and archived maps that NOAA does not keep). The Forensic view still offers the Prepare button first (web).
Past years list one river flood per gauge episode: a long river flood can appear as several entries numbered by name ('Rough River flood (KY, 2)').

PAST_RULE counts H-VTEC severity, which is NWS's forecast or observed severity (IEM's bulk route does not say which); the web's PAST_RULE_NOTE still says 'reached' until the integration changes it (R9).
A past reading's category is 'unknown' (NWS's category of a past reading is not kept; Fire-3d does not infer it). The Command hydrograph still labels it from today's thresholds (web).
Some NWS gauges have no USGS site in NWPS (e.g. Mississippi River at Hickman, HKMK2): no past readings, caveat NO_USGS_SITE.

Without a measured satellite image, a pass that NASA's catalog lists only after the first check following a build counts as new; one sensed before the build but listed late is taken as seen (it is not tried until a newer pass arrives).
The year lists are about 3 MB of JSON each (gzip about 0.4 MB); the web renders about 2,000 markers per year. Disk copies written before SCHEMA 2 are rebuilt once on the first request.
The new backend strings live in floods/history.py and floods/live.py (copy.py is not this role's file); the integration may move them and add them to CONTRACT 16.14.
The appended warnings.json / gauges.json reach an open Forensic view only after a reload (the web keys bundle files by built_ms; refreshed_ms is there for it).
The EARTHDATA_TOKEN path is still tested only with a fake token and a mock transport (not this role's code).
